title: Computation by the bridging machine
statement: Let $c$ be a program in the partial-recursive language, and let $f$ map Boolean strings to Boolean strings. Suppose that for every Boolean string $y$, evaluating $c$ on the singleton list containing the sentinel code of $y$ returns the singleton list containing the sentinel code of $f(y)$. Then, for every Boolean string $x$, there is a time $t$ at which the bridging machine of $c$, run on the input $x$, has halted and has output $f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: A program $c$ in the partial-recursive language
A function $f$ from Boolean strings to Boolean strings
For every Boolean string $y$, the specified evaluation of $c$ equals the singleton list containing the sentinel code of $f(y)$
replaced:
Let $c$ be a program in Mathlib's partial-recursive language and $f$ a total
function on Boolean strings such that, for every string $x$, evaluating $c$ on the
singleton list containing the sentinel numeric code of $x$ yields exactly the
singleton list containing the sentinel numeric code of $f(x)$.  Then for every $x$
there exists a time $t$ such that the bridging machine of $c$, run on the embedded
input $x$, halts within $t$ steps with the embedded string $f(x)$ on its output
tape.
